architecture.mechanism: Loss of LAIR1 inhibitory signaling causes excessive inflammatory tissue damage, driven by increased production of proinflammatory cytokines, myeloid chemokines, neutrophil ROS, and upregulation of collagen/ECM remodeling pathway proteins including collagens and complement factors.
architecture.intervention: Introduce a watchdog inhibitory signal pathway in the ECM brake controller that suppresses runaway signaling cascades from the stability control, traction control, and ABS subsystems, analogous to LAIR1's negative regulation of inflammatory responses, to prevent processor overload and non-response.
architecture.expected_effect: Brake function is restored while ABS and stability control remain enabled, and the "limited to 62 mph" limp-mode condition is avoided because the controller no longer enters a failure state triggered by excessive simultaneous subsystem demands.
architecture.falsification_test: On a 2019 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 bench rig, induce simultaneous illumination of check engine, stability control, traction control, and ABS warning indicators while driving at 60 mph; if the inhibitory signal mechanism is effective, the ECM processor must continue to deliver brake response commands and must not impose the 62 mph speed cap, and the test must be repeated across 100 thermal-stressed cycles without recurrence of processor non-response.
